description: Use VSCode's multi-file search to find all technical debt markers (TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX) across the codebase and create a structured markdown inventory document. Steps: (1) Open Search panel with Ctrl+Shift+F, (2) Enable regex mode by clicking the .* button, (3) Enter search pattern: (TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX): to match any debt marker followed by a colon, (4) In 'files to include' field enter: *.py, *.js, *.ts, *.jsx, *.tsx to focus on source files, (5) In 'files to exclude' field enter: **/node_modules/**, **/venv/**, **/dist/**, **/__pycache__/** to exclude dependencies, (6) Press Enter to execute search, (7) Review the ~10 search results showing file paths, line numbers, and comment text, (8) Create a new file named TECHNICAL_DEBT.md in the workspace root directory, (9) Structure the document with markdown headings: '# Technical Debt Inventory' as title, then organize findings into sections like '## Critical Issues (FIXME/HACK)', '## Deferred Work (TODO)', '## Security Concerns (XXX)', (10) For each debt marker found in search results, add an entry in checkbox format: '- [ ] File: <relative-path>, Line: <number> - <description>' where <relative-path> is the file path relative to workspace root (e.g., src/utils/cache.py), <number> is the line number, and <description> is the comment text or summary, (11) Ensure at least 6 out of the 10 debt markers present in the codebase are documented, (12) Add a Summary section at the end with total count, (13) Save the file with Ctrl+S. The workspace contains a multi-language project with Python (.py), JavaScript (.js), TypeScript (.ts/.tsx/.jsx) files across directories like src/, tests/, config/ with approximately 10 technical debt comments scattered throughout.
